Wording is verbatim, but s.3 in this form is the substitution made by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022 and cannot be applied directly to the 1994 deed; the transitional and validation provisions that govern a pre-2022 power at the matter date (28-2022 s.8 and 3-2024 s.6) were missing and have been added as PROV-M026-902 and PROV-M026-903. The corpus body also carries the subsection (1) marker only as "(a)", an OCR loss.

Wording is verbatim and supports the point that a notice of intended acquisition is given to the owner, but s.4 creates no right to obtain confirmation from the acquiring officer that no acquisition proceeding affects the land, which is the document the answer actually calls for; that step is conveyancing practice, not this section.

added_provisions.reason: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.4(3). The map supported the purchaser's shareholding documents with ss.2 and 3, which state a prohibition and its exemptions but require no document. s.4(3) is the provision that requires the company secretary to submit documentary proof of foreign shareholding before the Registrar of Lands will register the transfer, so it is what actually puts the share register and the annual return on the list. Cited in CL-M026-Q01-024.

Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022 s.8(1)(a) and (2). The map applied the 2022 substitution of s.3 of the Ordinance directly to a 1994 power of attorney. s.8 is the transitional provision that carries an unregistered pre-2022 power into the current regime and voids it if it was not submitted in time. Cited in CL-M026-Q01-016 and CL-M026-Q01-021.

Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 3 of 2024 s.6. It replaces the six-month window in 28-2022 s.8 with two years from 25 October 2022, so an unregistered pre-2022 power is null and void from 25 October 2024, inside the matter reference month. This is the sharpest temporal point in the matter and the map did not hold it. Cited in CL-M026-Q01-021.

Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.4(1)(c). CL-M026-Q01-021 asks for evidence that the power was unrevoked when the 1994 deed was signed; no cited provision supported that element. s.4(1)(c) requires a revocation to be registered in the folio with a cross reference to the power's own registration, which is how the absence of a revocation is established. Cited in CL-M026-Q01-021.

question_decisions.note: Every provision in the map checks out on wording and almost all on temporal applicability, and the enrichment is sound. The question is downgraded for two reasons. The answer's list of documents is partly a practice list: the depth of the search, the acquisition clearance, the street line and building limit confirmation, the bank's release letter and the fresh survey are not required by any corpus provision, so a complete answer does not follow from statute alone even though each document is given a statutory reason. And PROV-M026-006, an indispensable provision, exists only by virtue of the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024, whose commencement date is not in the corpus. authority_requirement is left at statute_only because the missing element is conveyancing practice, not case law; if a lawyer treats it as common law the question must be reclassified mixed_statute_and_case and reserved. Hop count 3 was checked against the reasoning edges and left unchanged; the four added provisions sit inside the existing three steps and do not create a fourth.

disagreements.researcher_position: statute_only and proposed_gold: every document called for is called for because a statutory provision makes it necessary, and the one practice element, the thirty-year look-back, is recorded in corpus_gaps and deliberately not asserted.
disagreements.verifier_position: The statutory hooks are real but the list itself is a conveyancing practice list. The answer asserts several documents that no corpus provision requires (confirmation from the acquiring officer, street line and building limit confirmation, the bank's letter of release, a fresh survey) and leaves the depth of the search unfixed. That makes it a gold answer a lawyer must sign off on the practice content of, not a statute-only gold answer, so needs_legal_review rather than proposed_gold.

disagreements.researcher_position: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(2)(a) is applicable at October 2024, with a note asking the verifier to confirm the commencement of Act No. 4 of 2024.
disagreements.verifier_position: The corpus cannot confirm it. Act No. 4 of 2024 has no commencement provision beyond its short title, so it operated from the date it became an Act, and the corpus holds no certification date. The only ground for treating it as in force by October 2024 is the inference that an Act numbered 4 of 2024 was certified early in that year. Marked partially_verified rather than unresolved on that basis.

unsupported_claims: CL-M026-Q01-007: states the stamping bar as absolute; 6-1990 s.60 has a proviso allowing admission in evidence, and action by the Registrar-General where the duty is Rs. 5,000 or less, on payment of the duty and a penalty. Marked disputed.
CL-M026-Q01-011: omits the closing words of Companies Act s.185(1)(d), which limit the articles limb to a provision included at incorporation. Marked disputed.

CL-M026-Q01-017 and CL-M026-Q01-027: Land Acquisition Act s.4 provides for a notice to the owner; it creates no right to obtain confirmation from the acquiring officer that no acquisition affects the land. Marked disputed.
CL-M026-Q01-022: Survey Act s.13 is an admissibility rule only; the recommendation of a fresh survey is a practice judgement, not a statutory requirement. Marked disputed.
CL-M026-Q01-023: no cited provision requires the bank's letter of release; Companies Act ss.102 and 105 support only the charge search. Marked disputed.

CL-M026-Q01-028 and CL-M026-Q01-029: the conclusions carry the practice items forward (search depth, fresh survey, release on completion, street line confirmation, retention from the price). Marked disputed.
CL-M026-Q01-013: correct on the current text but rests entirely on the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024, whose commencement is unverifiable here. Marked disputed.
temporal_issues: PROV-M026-006 (7-1840/s2(2)(a)) exists only because of Act No. 4 of 2024; no commencement date in the corpus, and the matter date is in the same year.

PROV-M026-005 quotes s.2(1)(a) as substituted by the same Act No. 4 of 2024, though the notarial requirement itself is unchanged in substance since 1840, so nothing in the answer turns on which text applies.

PROV-M026-021 (4-1902/s3) is the 28-2022 substitution and was applied to a 1994 deed without the transitional provisions; added as PROV-M026-902 and PROV-M026-903. The validation period in 3-2024 s.6 expires 25 October 2024, the matter reference month.

Registration of Documents (Amendment) Act No. 18 of 2024 was checked: it has a deferred commencement by Ministerial Order and repeals Chapter IV (ss.16 to 24), so it does not touch ss.7, 11, 14 or 42 relied on in the map.
Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 3 of 2024 was checked against 4-1902/s3: it amends ss.2, 3D and 4 and Schedule II, not s.3, so the researcher's account of s.3 is right as far as it goes.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: 38-2014/s4(3), the duty of the Registrar of Lands to require documentary proof of foreign shareholding from the company secretary; added as PROV-M026-901.
28-2022/s8 and 3-2024/s6, the transitional and validation provisions for pre-2022 powers of attorney; added as PROV-M026-902 and PROV-M026-903.
4-1902/s4(1)(c), registration of a revocation in the folio with a cross reference; added as PROV-M026-904.

23-1927/s32 (caveats) is not in the map. A registered caveat is disclosed by the same folio search the answer calls for and belongs in the encumbrance limb; not added because no claim in the gold answer mentions caveats and the verifier may not rewrite the answer prose.

23-1927/s13(1) and (7), the description of the land and the reference at the head of an instrument to the volume and folio of an earlier registered instrument, would support the demand for the prior deeds more directly than s.14 alone; not added for the same reason.

38-2014/s11 bars mortgaging land transferred under s.2(1) for five years from the transfer. It affects what the company may do after completion rather than what is called for now, but a lawyer advising this purchaser should be told.
case_law_dependence: The answer cites no case law and the validator's case-citation check passes.

The underlying practice content (a good root of title and the conventional look-back, the effect of a defective link on a later purchaser) is Roman-Dutch common law and conveyancing convention. The researcher kept it out of the answer prose, which is the right call, but it is why the answer reads as incomplete for a four-mark question.
enrichment_issues: Eleven added facts were checked. None names a statute or a section number and none states the conclusion; each synthetic_decisive fact has a reason and a counterfactual that names what falls away.

FACT-M026-Q01-002 bundles four facts (assessment number, Municipal Council limits, declared development area, year of construction) into one entry, so a lawyer cannot approve or reject the development-area limb separately from the municipal limb.

FACT-M026-Q01-011 states the completion month, which the matter_reference_date already fixes; harmless, but it is the fact that makes the power of attorney deadline in 3-2024 s.6 decisive, and its stated reason does not mention that.

FACT-M026-Q01-006 says the mortgage particulars were filed with the Registrar of Companies. That answers in advance part of what the charge search is for, which slightly softens the exercise, though it does not leak a statute or a section.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: PROV-M026-005 and PROV-M026-006 are both 7-1840/s2 with different subsections. That is permitted by the schema and the excerpts do not overlap, but any count of distinct sections in this map should treat them as one.
No question or provision duplicates another matter's content that this verifier can see; other matters' directories were not read.

lawyer_questions: Is a statute-only answer acceptable for an examination-of-title question, given that the depth of the search and several of the documents called for (acquisition clearance, street line and building limit confirmation, release of mortgage on completion) are conveyancing practice with no source in the corpus? If not, M026-Q01 should be reclassified mixed_statute_and_case and reserved rather than kept as a gold answer.

Was the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024 certified before October 2024? The whole of s.2(2), including the corporate-transferee proviso the answer relies on, depends on it, and the corpus holds no date.

Should the answer state the 25 October 2024 deadline in 3-2024 s.6 for registering the 1994 power of attorney? On the enriched facts completion falls in that month, which makes it the sharpest practical point in the matter.
Should a caveat search (23-1927 s.32) be named among the documents called for? It comes out of the same folio search the answer already requires.
